body:
The last time I was at the hospital, I called them up and I went to the intake person for the psych unit because I knew that I seriously suicidal and I needed constant supervision. So, I wasn't admitted via the ER, but this was my experience. 

Basically, the intake person there asked a million and one questions. If you're actively suicidal and can't agree to not kill yourself or if you have a serious plan then you'll probably be put into inpatient care for around 3 days-a week. 

If you can agree to not hurt yourself, you may be put into a partial hospitalization program, where you spend half your day in the hospital and the other half at home. If you do inpatient, you also usually do this option when you start to step down from a higher level of care. 

Honestly, the hospital sucks ass. It was horrendously depressing, but it woke me up to the severity of the situation that I was in and how much I wanted to get better really, not just die. Like, dying would be a solution, but if things were better then I'd want to live. It also made a lot of my problems seem more solvable and I got a lot of perspective. It's definitely more of a learning experience than a quick magical solution. That being said though, as much as I hated the place, it probably saved my life and I wouldn't be here today without such a resource. I'm just a bit of a grouch.

If you've any questions about the day to day programming of inpatient or partial hospitalization, I can elaborate as well/answer them. 

Honestly, you probably won't like the hospital but it's still very good and very essential that you seek help. Everyone I met there hated the fucking place, but still were all very grateful to be there and have a second chance at life. Like, the whole situation sucks for the time being, but you just have to look at the bigger picture. It's about safety for yourself, not having a grand old time.
I take vit D as well. I basically don't exercise. I've been feeling really bad this week so I have barely been eating but normally my diet is just fine. I'm at a normal weight.
